- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-0.mdx`  _(via ObjectStackProtocolImplementation (symbol, a top-level class))_

> `content/docs/releases/` is RELEASE-OWNED (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails"): release
> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- the SDK route bridge reached **54** of **206** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **11** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json fba37122b0f6646a3d8dd0b5384319e8bed3ae12` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `ef44c3beab7db1dd8f7a654b25715307fa27556f` — the merge of head `ee862ff9d0f4e5d3f23f75f918fcb3c026efed7b` into base `fba37122b0f6646a3d8dd0b5384319e8bed3ae12`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin ef44c3beab7db1dd8f7a654b25715307fa27556f && git checkout ef44c3beab7db1dd8f7a654b25715307fa27556f
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin fba37122b0f6646a3d8dd0b5384319e8bed3ae12 ee862ff9d0f4e5d3f23f75f918fcb3c026efed7b && git checkout -B drift-repro fba37122b0f6646a3d8dd0b5384319e8bed3ae12 && git merge --no-ff ee862ff9d0f4e5d3f23f75f918fcb3c026efed7b

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json fba37122b0f6646a3d8dd0b5384319e8bed3ae12
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs fba37122b0f6646a3d8dd0b5384319e8bed3ae12` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## 席位核对

ACCEPT · `domain:spec` seat 1 (#6017) · `huangyiirene` · session `session_01YRp5z4kK6vgYkrdH97ztsy` · head `ee862ff9d` · 2026-10-14T20:16Z

No contract face, so no review is owed beyond this one: no published schema, no governed text, `Clause-②: no`. CI and this seat's own read clear it. Card #23527, claim `6176390068`, dev report on #23527.

**1. Shape**
- Draft, base `main`. Line 1 `Fixes #23527`, line 2 `Clause-②: no`. No other closing keyword.
- 3 files, `+381 / -0`:
  - `protocol.ts` `+70`, the `duplicatePackage` region only: the docblock, `rewriteFieldRuleKeys` beside `deepRewrite`, and its call in the existing `permission` branch;
  - the new real-kernel pin;
  - the changeset.
- `reference-sites.ts` and `packages/spec/**` are untouched, as fenced.
- The step is keyed on the declared shape (the `fields` record of a copied `permission` item), not on a property name, so an object's own `fields` is never read.
- A collision `continue`s before `saveMetaItem`, so nothing is written for a refused set.
- The changeset is a `@objectstack/metadata-protocol` patch. Its FROM / TO / Unchanged paragraphs match the code.

**2. Premises measured**
- **H1 held:** `deepRewrite` renames a record key only under an object-reference property, and the free-text regex reads values, not keys. So both a prefixed and a bare object's `fields` keys stayed at base (the base run's copy keys equalled the source's).
- **H2:** the object part is everything before the first `.` (object and field names are both `^[a-z_][a-z0-9_]*$`). It is renamed only on an exact `renameMap` hit, and the field part is never read. Pinned: `ticket.ticket` → `dupdst_ticket.ticket`.
- **H3:** the enumeration is in the PR body. Only `PermissionSetSchema.fields` is fixed here; the other sites are out of scope (item 5).
- **H4 measured, not pinned:** `PermissionEvaluator.getFieldPermissions` and `FieldMasker.maskResults`, run on the stored copy. At head, the copy hides `full_name` and `secret` on the duplicate's objects. With the key rewrite ablated, it hides nothing. The order allowed a stored-key pin with the effect measured once, and that is what was done.

**3. Gates**
- Check-runs on `ee862ff9d` at this act: 22 success, 6 skipped, 10 in progress, 0 failures. The flip waits for green.
- Local: `--ran` over 67 families, 66 run. 1 is NOT MEASURED: `check:dual-build-cjs-loads`, exit 3, which needs a whole-workspace build. CI runs it.
- The real-kernel pin has 5 cases, each with a negative control. Results:
  - base (first fixture revision): 4 of 4 red;
  - head: 9 of 9 green, together with #23511's pin;
  - ablation on the key lookup: 5 failed, and the restore is proven.
- metadata-protocol: 28408 passed. objectql local: 8108 passed. Both typechecks exit 0, and the new file is in the test program.

**4. Deviations accepted**
- **The collision arm** (the dev's open question 2) is kept, beyond the card's three bullets. A renamed key that equals one the set already holds refuses the set in `failed[]` with both keys, never merging them. This seat's reading: either silent winner drops a security rule, which is the fail-open class this card closes. It matches PR #23525's refuse-never-reinvent posture, is measured reachable through the save door, and is one branch, one `failed[]` push and one pin case, adding no gate.
- **Landing before #23538 item 1** (the dev's open question 1, option A). A copied set with a rule on a field the object copy half-renames is now refused at the copy by `security-fls-unknown-field`. Before this PR, the same set copied with every rule fail-open. A loud refusal replaces a silent wrong result, and the cause is upstream (the field's key and `name` disagree), so it is fixed there, not by bending this rule (option C would contradict bullet 2). Neither question needs the maintainer: both are inside the card's scope and the rulings already standing.
- **The pin fixture moved after the base run:** the field-part case went from `dupsrc_customer.dupsrc_customer` to `ticket.ticket` / `dupsrc_customer.ticket` once item 1 was measured. The final fixture is red under ablation for the base reasons.
- **`main` is not merged.** One disjoint commit (`e1cefa58e`, hono adapter) landed after the base, and `merge-tree` is clean (#23405).

**5. Out of scope** (filed by this seat from the report; three cards, the per-fire quota)
- **#23537:** PR #23525's `objects` record-key rule silently merges a renamed key with one the set already holds, dropping a grant. In the measured case the copy gains edit and delete.
- **#23538** (one family card, two items):
  - the object copy gives a field named after a prefixed object a renamed `name` under its old key;
  - a bare object's view item keeps its `OBJECT.VIEWKEY` name, and the source shadows it on a no-package read.
- **#23539:** `findReferencesToMeta` ("Used by") misses a permission set that names an object only in its `fields` keys. `reference-sites.ts` was fenced here on purpose.
- **Acceptance note, carried by #23538** as its "noted, not measured" line: a view-item id inside a value keeps a bare object's name; read from the code.

**6. Landing:** Tier S, ordinary queue, once the head is all green.
